notes: Clean layering with a generic (names, dynamic) Placeholders() API and the policy in reverseproxy, plus a good detection table test; minor nits are returning the internal slice uncloned and a test whose buffered channel would hang rather than fail if the bug came back.

Keeps the layering of the reference by exposing generic placeholder names from caddyhttp, uses an explicit dynamic flag instead of an empty-string sentinel, keeps the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy, and adds a thorough table test of the detection plus end-to-end body/hit checks (minor: returns the internal slice without cloning).

Production code matches the reference: a generic Placeholders() accessor, with the response-placeholder policy kept in reverseproxy; tests cover the accessor, the ph() direct form via a parameterized status-code test, and request-only expressions.

Non-test code is essentially identical to the reference fix; the tests cover the Placeholders extraction, every request-only case named in the spec, and extend the existing status-code retry test to the direct ph() form.

Fix logic is correct but has the same layering issue as C1, and the new integration test is inserted between TestReverseProxyRetryMatchHeader and its doc comment, so that comment now describes the wrong function.

The AST-based detection is correct and covers literal, dynamic, escaped and look-alike placeholder names, but it hard-codes reverse-proxy placeholder names into the generic caddyhttp matcher, and the new integration test is inserted between TestReverseProxyRetryMatchHeader and its doc comment, so that comment now sits on the wrong function.

Correct AST-based detection that handles shorthand, direct ph() calls, escaped literals, near-miss names and dynamic names, but it puts reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher; tests are thorough and include the transport-error retry path.

Detection is correct, including dynamic names, escaped literals and prefix look-alikes, and the tests are strong (including that request-only expressions still gate transport-error retries), but reverse-proxy-specific placeholder knowledge now lives in the generic CEL matcher.

The squashfs side is fine, but zip hides every member stored beneath a symlink path, even without --links, with an O(n*m) prefix scan; this unrequested behavior change likely causes the hidden test failure.

The squashfs side closely matches the reference, but the zip side adds a quadratic pre-pass that silently hides every member stored under a symlink path, even without --links; this departs from the expected behaviour (the destination should refuse the write instead) and fails one hidden test.

Close to the reference for zip and squashfs, with a clamped seek and thorough tests (including a hostile-copy test), but a root pointing at a link must use the unsuffixed name, and squashfs now has two parallel lookup paths (newObjectNative and newObjectRemote).

Symlink listing, skipping and reading are clean and close to the reference in both backends, but a root pointing at a link only resolves under its native name, not its listed `.rclonelink` name, so single-object operations on links disagree with the listing.

Correct, with suffix-named root support and regular-file-wins collision handling, but the squashfs lookup refactor and zip pendingLinks/reserved bookkeeping add complexity, and the offset clamp now changes Open for all zip files.

Thorough handling of collisions and suffixed roots with a good escape test, but rewriting `newObjectNative` into `findNative` drops the `recoverParsePanic` guard on the NewObject path, it does not reset `pendingLinks` for single-object roots, and it changes the offset clamp for all zip files.

Works and handles name collisions, but zip eagerly opens and reads every symlink at mount (extra I/O on remote archives), squashfs.go has an unused maxLinkTargetSize constant, and the squashfs tests use os.Chdir and os.Symlink (fragile, not Windows-safe).

Functionally correct with collision handling, but zip eagerly opens every symlink member at list time (costly on remote storage), duplicates `openLink`/`maxLinkTargetSize` (the latter unused in squashfs), and its squashfs tests rely on `os.Chdir` and `os.Symlink`, which is fragile.

The storage-lookup approach works for gc, selected and stale compaction, clears the appender on both paths, and survives restart because replay repopulates the storage. Weaknesses: it uses an awkward variadic optional callback and adds an exported method, it ignores uncommitted exemplars, and its tests cover only head-truncate unit cases with no restart or selected/stale compaction coverage.

Retains series in both gc and gcSeries when the exemplar storage still holds an exemplar at or after minValidTime, releases chunks and clears the appender, and survives restart/snapshot because the storage is repopulated; however, the variadic 'optional callback' parameter is a compatibility hack, pending (uncommitted) exemplars are not protected unlike the reference, and the tests only cover head-level truncation, not selected/stale compaction or restart.

This candidate keeps exemplar series by looking up their labels in the circular exemplar storage, and it releases chunks in gcSeries correctly. However, it changes the unexported gc/gcSeries signatures, which likely breaks compilation of the hidden tests (0/3, suite failed). It also leaves the stale appender in place on the time-based gc path, and does not protect exemplars that are appended but not yet committed.

Functionally similar to C2 with good tests (including a storage unit test and restart cases), but it needlessly reorders gcSeries parameters and changes the gc signature, which breaks compilation against the upstream tests (0/3, suite failed), and it does not clear the appender for series retained in the ordinary gc path.

This is essentially the same design as C1, with thorough tests (restart, snapshot, zero/negative timestamps). The required-parameter signature changes break the hidden tests (0/3, suite failed). The gc path does not clear the stale appender, uncommitted exemplars are unprotected, and the releaseChunks comment wrongly claims chunk IDs stay unchanged.

Same storage-lookup approach with clean, well-documented code and strong DB-level tests (all three compaction paths, restart, snapshot, zero/negative timestamps), but changing the stripeSeries.gc/gcSeries signatures breaks the upstream test suite so all hidden tests and the package suite fail, and the gc path leaves the stale appender referencing the removed chunk.
